title: s.t.a.l.k.e.r.: call of pripyat
text: S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Call of Pripyat is a solid atmospheric survival horror fps that has a beautifully done open world with a variety of main and side quests. Solid shooting mechanics that are the most realistic you could get besides Arma. Plenty of weapons and armor to chose from. The graphics, whilst not the quality of the frostbite 3 or cryengine 3, are great with all the options you could ever need. Except for a field of view option, which is lacking in all 3 S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games, but you may download a mod which has an fov option. With multiple endings to the game, this can give you lots of replayability. To extend the game even more, you can download many mods that can improve the graphics or make the game a whole lot scarier than it already is. Speaking of which. Combined with the atmospheric environment and the dangerous npcs and mutants that you will run into can make a journey during the night an intense and fun experience. There are 3 small open worlds within the game to create this environment that you can explore that very few games achieve. There are many more mechanics that I'm not going to list so this review doesn't become very long. But I will list a few negatives that I have with this game, 1st the npcs are more bland than a cardboard box except for a few. The dialogue tree is basic with limited options. If you go to explore the open world if you chose to stay at the end of the game. Exploring will become stale eventually. Along with being much smaller than the other 2 games. Leaving you coming back to this game less often. And with a gtx 970 the game can't stay a stable 60fps on medium settings with the game looking like it can out in 2005. But at $20 this game is definitely worth it, or even better if it's on sale.

title: s.t.a.l.k.e.r.: call of pripyat
text: TL;DR Like fallout 3, but improves on it in every way. Instead of having to choose between to black and white factions (enclave and brotherhood of steel). THE FACTIONS Fallout: New Vegas provides 4 unique and diverse main factions you can join. The New California Republic, Ceasers Legion, Mr, House, and a secret option (i'll just say it's a wild card). They all have hidden agendas that could or could not be helpful to the people of the mojave wasteland. The NCR, for example, is a faction that is trying to rebuild a democratic nation much like 1800s America. But, if you ask around NCR soldiers and workers, you discover that they are extremely corrupt and are at risk of being beaten by Ceasers Legion, a group of slavers that know how to create a very stable society. FO:NV, aside from the 4 main factions, features a number of other smaller factions. They include the Followers of the Apocolypse, The Brotherhood of Steel, The Great Khans, The Boomers, and another faction that is hidden. PLAYER FREEDOM FO:NV may not give you the freedom to do as many things as in Skyrim or Fallout 4, but the player can have a huge influence on the mojave wasteland. By far the way to play the game and get the most freedom, is by leveling up your speech skill. You can convince people and factions to do a huge number of things with a high speech. Don't want the Great Khans fighting for The Legion? A high speech skill can dictate how effective your attempt at convincing them is. Obsidian has done a great job at providing diplomatic options for the player to take. THE ISSUES FO:NV, as great as it is, has some big issues. The gunplay is not a very good mechanic. The bandits in this game, although they are divided into seperate extremely small factions, you can't interact with them. You do not have the option to be the bad guy on some quests. Some DLC *cough* Old World Blues *cough* can be boring to do and extremely limited in the ammount of content. Luckily, the game does not have many bugs though.

text: Installing and running this game takes a little bit of tweaking as it will not run with later versions of PhysX. It's simple though, uninstall PhysX in Control Panel>Add/Remove Programs, then use the PhysX install file which is in the game folder, or download legacy drivers from Nvidia. I also have it running in WinXP SP3 mode, though I did this before reconfiguring PhysX so not sure if necessary. **The camera on default settings is annoying! Others have pointed this out but it's easy fixed. It moves for you at the worst angles. Don't worry though, three clicks in settings under Camera (untick them all) and you can control the camera angle yourself using A and D keys, and mouse wheel to zoom. Having said that, for 5 minutes of tweaking, this game is totally worth it. If you like Diablo, The Elder Scrolls, played the first Sacred or simply love RPG type "kill, level, loot" games, you will love this. The map is huge and free to roam at your Leisure. Everywhere you go there is something to battle and loot. You barely need to buy armour or anything because you can loot everything you need, unless buying something specific. So many hours of gameplay, side quests, main story quests, random exploration, whatever you want. Choose your character based roughly on the type of game you would like to play, for example, follow the "light" or "dark" path, choose a character based on their fighting styles, once in game the skills you give your character can complement the base skills you have or you can train something totally unique. I could go on, but, just buy it. It's cheap and with so much to do and so many ways to do it, you will get your moneys worth. I would go so far to say this game is essential for RPG lovers. Yes I would.

title: saints row 2
text: This game has really amazing world, story and things to do. Also got many problems. First of all, it crashes a loooooooooooooooooooot! Doesn't matter how much you advanced, unlocked, or even completed the missions, game will crash and your effort which should be more than at least hours will become nothing. Second, if you are not doing story related missions, NOTHING will be saved unless you manually save. So if you are doing any extra missions or mics activities to get reputation, nothing will be saved automatically. What if you just got some unlocks and games crashes like how I mentioned at the first problem? You will lose everything except the main story line.. What if you forgot to save manually or on next day choose "continue" than "load" game? You will lose everything except the main story line. This forced me to play same thing multiple times untill I found out the problem. Third, this is PC platform but on game menu you will not be able to use mouse courser. Think about playing Starcraft without mouse. PC platform without hotkey settings and mouse courser is something like that. Forth, the physical movements are so bad. I understand this is oooooold game, but got hit by a small piece of metal from exploded car, from the direction you can't see make your character fly and roll to the ground, then ran over by cars around you again again again utill the death is not fun. This also will force you to play same thing repeatedly, which will bring you a disaster if the game crashed or you just forgot to save the game manually. Moreover, sometimes the display goes black but game is still running. You will hear the sounds, which is your charater is dying. This becomes a pain when you are just about to finish the lv6 activities and unlock something. It will happen a lot. There are more problems than I can write now, but not because of difficulty because of the bad interface, game system, bugs and access make the game harder than you think. This game quite impressed me more than old GTA series, but how they put it on PC platform is so horrible. I would say this game must be free to play now and must share source like open source SW. That will help people to create fixes or user patches. How much developers dedicated for ingame story and actions are waaaaay better than actual system, layout, interface or more cons. Advice? Just skip SR2 and play from SR3. SR3 at least goes way better for those aspects. (Instead, I prefer the SR2's story.)

I'm assuming that's due to the fact that I do not have a namebrand gamepad. The problem is that it worked at first. Then it didn't work after that. For example, I can use the D-Pad to move, but not for any of the bindings. SO annoying. So I can't use food/drinks and can't recruit (unless I use the keyboard). Some buttons I haven't been able to figure out what the gamepad equivalent even is. "R" to pick up doesn't see to be bound at all and can't figure out what it should be. it's really quite obnoxious. That being said, the game is crazy fun and I still feel the need to play it to move on with the story. They really could have done a better job with the PC port for this game though. Seriously. CONSTANT issues. I wouldn't receommend playing this game unless you can deal with the port issues and only then if you really are playing it for the storyline.

title: saints row iv
text: Oh dear god they jumped the shark...and its glorious! So in if you though the last game got crazy then buckle up becaue we have just hit an insanity singularity.  Saints Row IV starts with you saving america from a nuke (it only gets sillier from here) and becoming the president of the united states.  And then Aliens invade (told you) and kinap a bunch of the population incliding the saints.  Your stuck inside a computer simulation a'la the matrix and have to find away to escape and kick some alien♥♥♥♥♥ So by now you know what to expect.  Open city to explore and tear up, funny writting, lots of side missions yada yada.  so whats new in this one?  Super Powers.  While in the simulation you now have access to super powers like super speed, the ability to jump buildings and glide for miles, telekinises, the ablity to shoot fire and ice.  All sorts of crazy stuff. and it is so much fun.  Nothing beats running up a building, jumping off, gliding half way across the city and landing on a group of aliens before freezing the surviors before blowing them to icy chunks.  And the new side quests are all designed around your powers.  and you'll need to do them too becaue the upgrade system from the 3rd game is back so cash and experince are important as is are the glowing collectables littered all over the city which are used to upgrade your powers. Customization is about what it was in the 3rd game...in fact most of it is copied from the 3rd game.  This was originally planned to be an expansion to Saints row the Third but they turned it into its own game.  So alot of assets from the 3rd game are reused in this one.  Not a huge flaw considering how different the gameplay feels thanks to the powers. The only other complaint i have is that there really is little reason to use guns or cars now and yet you can still upgrade you weapons and trick out your rides. hell theres even a side quest that involves stealing new vehicles to add to your garage.  Now you can actually get some use out of guns if you want to play that way but there isn't a vehicle in the game thats better than your starting powers so why bother?  Again not a big deal. Small complaints aside this game is amazing fun and is chocked full of nerd culture refernces and over the top goodness.  Play, Destroy, Enjoy!!!  Strike a pose.

title: saints row iv
text: As fun as many of the super powers are and as wacky as some of the weapons are I think I liked SR3 slightly better. The story is decent but late game SR4 even makes fun of itself on stretching out the story, with events from SR1, 2, and 3 occuring in missions. I've played through it several times trying different combinations (Unlocking everything, only using base powers, not doing any side missions, etc.) and I've found that no matter the difficulty you need the experience and money from side missions (which are all activities) to upgrade yourself and weapons whereas the powers make certain areas easier except that there are a lot of ways the missions will temporary take away your powers. There are no decisions to make in SR4 that really encourage replayability like there were in SR3 and even with not having done coop on either game I've played SR4 about 50 hours less than SR3. There is more activity variety in SR4 but many of them offer only 3 (sometimes 6) instances and it can be easy to gold level them on the first try once you know what you're doing so it doesn't take long to go through the fun activities. The garage is mostly useless due to the running and flying abilities with those times when you want a vehicle it's easiest to just steal one. Rampages aren't as fun, except in missions/activities, and once you reach level 3 threat there is pretty much no way to get rid of the threat besides starting a mission/activity, portaling out, or fighting until it maxes and sends out a Warden. All in all it's a fun game with some of the missions being some of the best in the series while others are tedious. The DLC offers a decent return so it's worth it to pick up the GOTC version. I haven't played GOOH yet though I'll probably pick it up one sale some time. I can recommend it even if I still like Stilwater (from 1 and 2) over Steelport (3 and 4) and that SR2 was the game I had the most fun exploring.
